messages:
sre_lead: Heads up — we’re seeing intermittent packet loss on the SFO <-> EU-West peering link, started ~1913456700. Impacting provisioning APIs and causing GPU attach failures for a subset of Dedicated pools.
oncall-bot: ALERT: network.packet_loss detected between sfo-edge-1 and eu-west1 (severity: high). Incident created: INC-20260318-87
oncall: Confirmed. Control plane shows elevated API latencies and a backlog in the provisioning queue. Some traffic already shifted to us-west1 via smart routing; that is causing queueing there.
maria: Checking underlying infra now. BGP sessions briefly flapped on the SFO transit provider, looks like 4x withdraws in the last 7m. Dumping peer logs.
devon: If we keep shifting traffic to us-west1, tokenized customers on committed pools will see degraded latency. We should throttle automated routing and prefer regional failover only for best-effort tiers.
sre_lead: Agreed. Can we draft a short customer-facing blurb for Statuspage and Support? Need ETA for next update and mitigation plan.
support_ops: Draft below. Thoughts?\n\n[STATUSPAGE DRAFT]\nWe are investigating an issue affecting provisioning and inference latency for some customers between SFO and EU-West.\nImpact: provisioning failures and intermittent degraded performance in affected regions.\nScope: subset of Dedicated pools and some Hosted API requests.\nCurrent status: investigating, routing mitigations applied.\nNext update: in 30 minutes or as we have new info.\n\nPlease advise on wording / ETA. :+1:
product_pm: Keep it concise, call out "no data loss" and include expected customer-facing ETA if we have one.
maria: Mitigation path: ask transit to abort the flapping route, and we’ll briefly drain SFO ingress and fail traffic to alternate regions while monitoring. Should have a stabilization window estimate of ~20-40m if transit cooperates.
devon: Technical note for support: advise customers on Dedicated: pin to region or request manual re-provision if they need immediate placement (we can prioritize). For Hosted customers, auto-failover will continue but latency may be higher.
support_ops: Updated draft with no-data-loss note and ETA 40m. Pasting final copy for Statuspage and a shorter blurb for high-touch customers.\n\n[STATUSPAGE FINAL]\nWe’re investigating network instability between SFO and EU-West affecting provisioning and latency. No data loss has been detected. We have applied routing mitigations; we expect stabilization within ~40 minutes. We will provide updates every 30 minutes and notify high-touch customers directly.
statusbot: Posted update to status.redwood.ai — Incident INC-20260318-87: Network instability (SFO <-> EU-West). Next update scheduled 30 minutes.
sre_lead: Thanks team. support_ops, please begin outreach to the three customers flagged as high-touch and add any escalations to the ticket. maria/devon, keep me posted on transit response and whether we need to introduce manual failover.
maria: Transit acknowedged, they’re running route debug now. If the flaps stop we’ll bring SFO back to normal traffic within ~15m of stabilization. If flaps continue we’ll escalate to manual traffic shift and extend ETA.
oncall: Noted. Monitoring dashboards updated, I’ll push another status update at 1913458589 or earlier if we have resolution. :eyes:
